powertrains.notes: First-generation 2.7L EcoBoost (325 hp/375 lb-ft @ 3,000 rpm), unchanged 2015-2017, paired only with the 6R80 6-speed.

Second-generation 2.7L EcoBoost for MY2018: torque up to 400 lb-ft @ 2,750 rpm and the 10R80 10-speed became standard. Output unchanged through 2020; carries into the 2021 (14th-gen) F-150 essentially unchanged.
First-generation 3.5L EcoBoost (365 hp/420 lb-ft @ 2,500 rpm), 2015-2016, on the 6R80 6-speed.

Second-generation 3.5L EcoBoost (375 hp/470 lb-ft @ 3,500 rpm) launched for MY2017 paired exclusively with the all-new 10R80 10-speed -- a full model year before the 2.7L and 5.0L received the 10-speed in MY2018. Excludes the Limited-only High-Output 3.5L (450 hp/510 lb-ft), which is a trim-exclusive engine outside this catalog's scope.
Second-generation 5.0L Coyote V8 (385 hp/387 lb-ft @ 3,850 rpm), 2015-2017, on the 6R80 6-speed.
Third-generation 5.0L Coyote V8 for MY2018 gained port+direct injection (395 hp/400 lb-ft @ 4,500 rpm) and standard 10R80 10-speed.

3.0L Power Stroke diesel V6 introduced for MY2018 (250 hp @ 3,250 rpm / 440 lb-ft @ 1,750 rpm), paired exclusively with the 10R80 10-speed. Heaviest and least powerful engine in the lineup, but with the earliest, broadest torque plateau.
Base 3-valve V8 in its final two model years; adequate power but the least capable tow engine of this generation before EcoBoost/Coyote arrived.
Ford's long-serving 5.4L V8 in its final F-150 application; figures here are the SAE-net gasoline rating (the flex-fuel E85 rating is higher, 320 hp/390 lb-ft).
Twin-turbo V6 introduced for 2011 with a broad low-rpm torque plateau; matched the Coyote V8 on power while beating every gas engine in the lineup on torque and low-end response.
All-new for 2011, replacing the 4.6/5.4 as the mainstream V8; a truck-specific cam profile trades the Mustang Coyote's high-rpm output for more low/mid-range torque.
Optional heavy-duty V8, standard on SVT Raptor and Harley-Davidson and offered on Lariat Limited/Lariat/Platinum; the largest-displacement, highest-torque engine in this generation's F-150 lineup.

4.6L Triton V8, SOHC 2-valve: 231 hp @ 4,750 rpm / 293 lb-ft @ 3,500 rpm for 2004-2006, bumped to 248 hp / 294 lb-ft for 2007-2008 (this curve models the original 2004-2006 rating); paired only with the 4R70E 4-speed automatic.

5.4L Triton V8, SOHC 3-valve with variable cam timing: 300 hp @ 5,000 rpm / 365 lb-ft @ 3,750 rpm, unchanged across the full 2004-2008 run; standard on FX4/Lariat/King Ranch and up, paired only with the 4R75E 4-speed automatic (no 6-speed offered this generation).
Base-generation V8, rated 220 hp/290 lb-ft for nearly the whole run; some late trucks may carry a 231 hp/293 lb-ft rating.
Early 5.4L Triton rating, used 1997-1998 before the 1999 power bump.
Higher-output 5.4L Triton rating used from 1999 through the end of the generation in 2003.

195 hp @ 4,000 rpm / 275 lb-ft @ 3,000 rpm for automatic-equipped trucks (1994-96 Ford brochure figures; manual-transmission trucks were rated 205 hp at the same torque). 1992-93 trucks carried over the 1988-91-spec EFI 5.0L rated 185 hp @ 3,800 rpm / 270 lb-ft @ 2,400 rpm - noticeably milder than 1994-96. This entry models the 1994-96 automatic-transmission calibration as representative since the catalog only models the E4OD automatic. SuperCab 4x4, short/standard bed only (no crew cab existed on the 9th-gen F-150).

210 hp @ 3,600 rpm / 325 lb-ft @ 2,800 rpm for 1994-96, explicitly quoted from the period Ford brochure 'with Automatic Transmission.' Figures moved around across the run: 1992 was 210 hp/315 lb-ft, 1993 dipped to 200 hp/310 lb-ft (roller lifters/cam were introduced for 1994, coinciding with the return to 210 hp and a bump to 325 lb-ft). This entry models the 1994-96 automatic-transmission calibration as representative. SuperCab 4x4, short/standard bed only (no crew cab existed on the 9th-gen F-150).
Base dual-motor powertrain with the standard-range battery; full torque available from rest, tapering to constant power above roughly 3,050 rpm.

Higher-output dual-motor powertrain paired with the extended-range battery; same 775 lb-ft peak torque as Standard Range but stretched to more power via a constant-power taper starting near 3,950 rpm.

powertrains.engineName: High-Output 6.7L Power Stroke V8 Turbo Diesel

powertrains.notes: 6.2L SOHC 2V 'Boss' V8, essentially unchanged 2017-2022 including through the 2020 mid-cycle refresh. Confirmed via multiple 2020-era sources that it stayed on the 6R140-based TorqShift-G 6-speed for the whole generation -- it did NOT move to the 10R140 (unlike the diesel and the new-for-2020 7.3L gas engine), so this is modeled as a single powertrain entry rather than two.

New-for-MY2020 7.3L OHV 2V 'Godzilla' gas V8, standard 10R140 10-speed. Same 430 hp/475 lb-ft rating that continues unchanged into the 2023+ generation already in this catalog (engineName matches that entry exactly so the UI can carry the selection across generations).

Second-generation 6.7L Power Stroke on the 6R140 6-speed. CORRECTION to brief: MY2017 actually launched at 440 hp @ 2,800 rpm / 925 lb-ft @ 1,800 rpm (confirmed directly from Ford's own 2017 Super Duty brochure cover page); MY2018-2019 were recalibrated up to 450 hp / 935 lb-ft at the same rpm points. Modeled here at the 450/935 MY2018-2019 rating per the brief's own instruction, with the weaker 440/925 MY2017 figure called out here rather than as a separate entry.

2020 refresh: larger single sequential turbo, forged steel pistons, strengthened cylinder head, 36,000 psi common-rail injection, and the new 10R140 10-speed. 475 hp @ 2,800 rpm / 1,050 lb-ft @ 1,600 rpm -- an identical rating to the 2023+ standard-output Power Stroke already in this catalog, so the torque curve is reused verbatim from that entry per instructions.

Standard gas engine, 2011-2016 F-250/F-350 SRW, unchanged across the generation. 385 hp @ 5,500 rpm / 405 lb-ft @ 4,500 rpm applies to trucks under 10,000 lb GVWR, which covers all F-250/F-350 SRW pickup configurations. Ford's spec sheets also list a de-rated calibration (316 hp @ 4,179 rpm / 397 lb-ft @ 4,179 rpm) for chassis over 10,000 lb GVWR (F-350 DRW/F-450/F-550 cab-chassis) — not applicable to the SRW pickups modeled here. Curb weight and tire size are for a Crew Cab 4x4 SRW with the standard 6.75 ft box, XLT-equivalent trim.

MY2011 launched at 390 hp @ 2,800 rpm / 735 lb-ft @ 1,600 rpm; Ford issued a no-charge dealer PCM reflash within the 2011 model year that raised output to 400 hp / 800 lb-ft. That 400/800 rating is what shipped for the balance of 2011 production and for MY2012-2014, and is the rating modeled here (early-build 2011 trucks at 390/735 are not separately modeled). Twin-turbo 'DualBoost' (GT32) setup, replaced by the single GT37 VGT for 2015. Curb weight and tire size are for a Crew Cab 4x4 SRW with the standard 6.75 ft box, XLT-equivalent trim.

2015 model-year revision: replaced the twin GT32 'DualBoost' turbo with a single larger GT37 variable-geometry turbo, added a Bosch CP4.2 high-pressure fuel pump (longer stroke) and piezo fuel injectors, and IROX-coated lower main bearings, raising output to 440 hp @ 2,800 rpm / 860 lb-ft @ 1,600 rpm. No significant powertrain calibration change for 2016. Curb weight and tire size are for a Crew Cab 4x4 SRW with the standard 6.75 ft box, XLT-equivalent trim; curb weight bumped slightly (+50 lb) versus the 2011-2014 diesel entry for the larger turbo/cooling hardware — this delta is a low-confidence estimate.
The base V8 for '08-'10 Super Duty — adequate for light-duty use but the weakest tow engine of this trio.
The volume gas engine of this generation — a real torque step up from the 5.4 without the diesel's weight or price.
The heaviest and strongest option by far — a sequential twin-turbo diesel with a broad, flat torque plateau built for towing.

1999-2004 Super Duty-tuned 2-valve 5.4L, 260 hp @ 4,500 rpm / 350 lb-ft @ 2,500 rpm for the bulk of the run (very early 1999 trucks were 255 hp). Replaced by the 24-valve 3-valve 5.4L (300 hp/365 lb-ft) for 2005-2007, not modeled here per the brief.
1999-2004 20-valve V10, 310 hp @ 4,250 rpm / 425 lb-ft @ 3,250 rpm, matching the brief exactly. Replaced by the 30-valve 3-valve V10 for 2005.
2005-2007 3-valve V10 (355 hp / 455 lb-ft); Wikipedia's 362/457 figure belongs to the 2008-2010 trucks.

Automatic-transmission rating for the bulk of the 1999-2003 run: 250 hp @ 2,600 rpm / 505 lb-ft @ 1,600 rpm. Very early 1999 (pre running-change) autos were lower at 235 hp/500 lb-ft, and manual-transmission trucks were rated higher (275 hp/525 lb-ft) -- neither modeled here per the brief's instruction to use the representative automatic calibration.

2003-2007 replacement for the 7.3L, single rating across auto/manual. Modeled at the 2005-2007 calibration, 325 hp @ 3,300 rpm / 570 lb-ft @ 2,000 rpm; 2003-2004 trucks were slightly lower at 560 lb-ft, per the brief's instruction.

Brief's '~200-210 hp, 310-328 lb-ft' was directionally right but not a distinct 'HD' calibration split from F-150 in any source found; year-to-year running changes are what moved the number. Modeled 210 hp @ 3600 rpm / 325 lb-ft @ 2800 rpm, representative of 1994-1997 (majority of the run); 1992 ran ~210 hp/315 lb-ft and 1993 dipped to ~200 hp/310 lb-ft per secondary sources, so early-run trucks may read a touch lower than this curve.

1994-1997 EFI rating: 245 hp @ 4000 rpm / 410 lb-ft @ 2200 rpm (upper end of brief's stated range; used as the representative figure since it covers most of the run). Correction: 1992-1993 trucks were lower, commonly cited as 230 hp / 390 lb-ft, not modeled separately here. 1997 was the last model year the 460 was offered in the F-250.

Factory Garrett T3 turbo IDI (mechanical Stanadyne DB2 injection, 21.5:1 compression) was offered 1993 (mid-year, sometimes cited as '1993.5')-1994 only, exactly as the brief flagged. 190 hp @ 3000 rpm / 390 lb-ft @ 1400 rpm confirmed by two independent sources. The naturally-aspirated 7.3L IDI (185 hp @ 3000 rpm / ~358-360 lb-ft @ 1400 rpm, 21.5:1 CR, no turbo) ran 1988-1994 alongside/before it and is NOT modeled here per the brief's instruction.

HEUI-injected Garrett TP38 turbo (no intercooler until 1999), launched mid-1994 ('1994.5'). Modeled at the launch rating of 210 hp @ 3000 rpm / 425 lb-ft @ 2000 rpm, used as the representative E4OD-automatic figure for the full 1994.5-1997 run per the brief's instruction to model the automatic. CORRECTION/FLAG: secondary sources do NOT converge on the brief's specific claim of a clean 210/425-automatic vs 225/450-manual split for 1996-97 -- see confidenceNotes.

powertrains.engineName: High-Output 6.7L Power Stroke V8 Turbo Diesel

powertrains.notes: 6.2L SOHC 2V 'Boss' V8, essentially unchanged 2017-2022 including through the 2020 mid-cycle refresh. Confirmed via multiple 2020-era sources that it stayed on the 6R140-based TorqShift-G 6-speed for the whole generation -- it did NOT move to the 10R140 (unlike the diesel and the new-for-2020 7.3L gas engine), so this is modeled as a single powertrain entry rather than two.

New-for-MY2020 7.3L OHV 2V 'Godzilla' gas V8, standard 10R140 10-speed. Same 430 hp/475 lb-ft rating that continues unchanged into the 2023+ generation already in this catalog (engineName matches that entry exactly so the UI can carry the selection across generations).

Second-generation 6.7L Power Stroke on the 6R140 6-speed. CORRECTION to brief: MY2017 actually launched at 440 hp @ 2,800 rpm / 925 lb-ft @ 1,800 rpm (confirmed directly from Ford's own 2017 Super Duty brochure cover page); MY2018-2019 were recalibrated up to 450 hp / 935 lb-ft at the same rpm points. Modeled here at the 450/935 MY2018-2019 rating per the brief's own instruction, with the weaker 440/925 MY2017 figure called out here rather than as a separate entry.

2020 refresh: larger single sequential turbo, forged steel pistons, strengthened cylinder head, 36,000 psi common-rail injection, and the new 10R140 10-speed. 475 hp @ 2,800 rpm / 1,050 lb-ft @ 1,600 rpm -- an identical rating to the 2023+ standard-output Power Stroke already in this catalog, so the torque curve is reused verbatim from that entry per instructions.

Standard gas engine, 2011-2016 F-250/F-350 SRW, unchanged across the generation. Same 385 hp / 405 lb-ft rating and gearbox as the F-250; no F-250-vs-F-350 difference found in Ford's factory spec sheet for this engine's output or axle/gear ratios. Curb weight is slightly higher than the F-250 (heavier frame/springs); tire size and axle/gear ratios are identical between the two trucks per Ford's documentation. Curb weight and tire size are for a Crew Cab 4x4 SRW with the standard 6.75 ft box, XLT-equivalent trim.

Same MY2011 launch-then-reflash history as the F-250 entry (390/735 launch, reflashed to 400/800 within MY2011; 400/800 used here for MY2011-2014). F-350 SRW crew cab GVWR options extend meaningfully higher than F-250 SRW (up to ~11,500 lb per Ford's payload tables) to preserve payload with the heavier diesel engine. Curb weight and tire size are for a Crew Cab 4x4 SRW with the standard 6.75 ft box, XLT-equivalent trim.

Same 2015 GT37 turbo/injector/fuel-pump revision as the F-250 entry, raising output to 440 hp @ 2,800 rpm / 860 lb-ft @ 1,600 rpm. Curb weight and tire size are for a Crew Cab 4x4 SRW with the standard 6.75 ft box, XLT-equivalent trim.
The base V8 for '08-'10 Super Duty — adequate for light-duty use but the weakest tow engine of this trio.
The volume gas engine of this generation — a real torque step up from the 5.4 without the diesel's weight or price.
The heaviest and strongest option by far — a sequential twin-turbo diesel with a broad, flat torque plateau built for towing.
Same engine/rating as the F-250 entry: 260 hp @ 4,500 rpm / 350 lb-ft @ 2,500 rpm for 1999-2004 (very early 1999 was 255 hp). Replaced by the 24-valve 3-valve 5.4L for 2005-2007, not modeled here.
Same engine/rating as the F-250 entry: 1999-2004, 310 hp @ 4,250 rpm / 425 lb-ft @ 3,250 rpm.
2005-2007 3-valve V10 (355 hp / 455 lb-ft); Wikipedia's 362/457 figure belongs to the 2008-2010 trucks.

Same engine/rating as the F-250 entry: automatic-rated 250 hp @ 2,600 rpm / 505 lb-ft @ 1,600 rpm for the bulk of 1999-2003 (early 1999/2000 lower, manual higher -- not modeled). This is the classic 1-ton Crew Cab 4x4 diesel combo of the era.
Same engine/rating as the F-250 entry: 2003-2007, modeled at the 2005-2007 calibration of 325 hp @ 3,300 rpm / 570 lb-ft @ 2,000 rpm (2003-2004 was 560 lb-ft).

Same engine/rating as the F-250 entry (210 hp @ 3600 rpm / 325 lb-ft @ 2800 rpm, representative of 1994-1997; 1992 ~210/315, 1993 dipped to ~200/310). F-350 defaults to the 4.10 axle (more common on 1-ton than 3.55) per Ford towing-guide consensus.

Same engine/rating as the F-250 entry (245 hp @ 4000 rpm / 410 lb-ft @ 2200 rpm for 1994-1997; 1992-1993 lower at ~230/390, not separately modeled). Popular F-350 gasser of the era for its low cost/high torque vs the diesel option.
Same engine/rating as the F-250 entry. Offered 1993(.5)-1994 only before the Power Stroke replaced it mid-1994; NA IDI (185 hp/~358-360 lb-ft) not modeled per brief instruction.

Same engine/rating and same 1996-97 uprate ambiguity as the F-250 entry -- see confidenceNotes. This is the flagship OBS heavy-duty combo (Crew Cab 4x4 SRW + 7.3 diesel); Crew Cab body was F-350-only in this generation, matching the brief's premise.
2024+ TurboMax figures (430 lb-ft); 2019-2021 version made 348 lb-ft

powertrains.engineName: 5.3L V8 (L84, EcoTec3 w/ Dynamic Fuel Management)
powertrains.notes: 10-speed standard since 2024; launch trucks used an 8-speed

powertrains.engineName: 6.2L V8 (L87, EcoTec3 w/ Dynamic Fuel Management)
3.0L Duramax I6 Diesel (LZ0, current; earlier LM2)
powertrains.notes: 2023+ LZ0 figures (495 lb-ft); 2020-2022 LM2 made 460 lb-ft

Standard L83/6L80 pairing across the whole K2 generation (2014-2018), all trims. Factory final-drive options 3.08 (standard)/3.23/3.42, plus 3.73 with the Max Trailering Package. 355 hp @ 5,600 rpm / 383 lb-ft @ 4,100 rpm, unchanged 2014-2018.

8L90 became optional with the 5.3L on LTZ, LTZ Z71, and High Country trims starting MY2016 (not offered with the 5.3L in 2014-2015; the 6.2L got the 8-speed first, in 2015). Same 355 hp/383 lb-ft rating as the 6-speed truck; commonly bundled with the Max Trailering Package (3.42 or 3.73 axle).

8L90 paired with the 6.2L L86 from MY2015 on (the 2014 launch year used a 6L80 6-speed with the 6.2L instead, at the same 420 hp/460 lb-ft rating; not modeled as a separate entry since it's a single niche year). 6.2L offered only on Double Cab/Crew Cab, LTZ trim and above. 3.23 standard axle, 3.42 with Max Trailering Package (12,000 lb max tow, 2WD Crew Cab).
Base V8, fuel-economy oriented; never paired with the 6-speed automatic, and factory output rose modestly (295 to 302 hp) partway through the run.
Volume mid-range V8, paired exclusively with the 4-speed automatic through the 2009 model year.
Same 5.3L V8 gains the 6-speed automatic and a revised (VVT-enabled) torque calibration starting with the 2010 model year.
High-output V8, standard on GMC Sierra Denali and optional on top Silverado/Sierra trims from 2009 on; always paired with the 6-speed automatic.

Base V8 for extended-cab 4x4 GMT800 half-tons, rated 270 hp/285 lb-ft for MY2000-2003 (the MY1999 launch tune was a lower 255 hp, and MY2004+ trucks moved to a revised 285 hp/295 lb-ft version not modeled here).

Volume-selling V8 for GMT800 half-tons, rated 285 hp/325 lb-ft for MY2000-2003 (the MY1999 launch tune was a lower 270 hp/315 lb-ft, and MY2004+ trucks moved to a revised 295 hp/330 lb-ft version not modeled here).

Throttle-body-injected 350ci small block, RPO L05. Advertised 210 hp @ 4000 rpm / 300 lb-ft @ 2800 rpm (SAE net), consistent across 1992-1995. 1992-93 trucks used the non-electronic 4L60 (same gear ratios as 4L60-E); 4L60-E (electronic) phased in through 1993-94.

Vortec 5700, RPO L31: center-bolt valve covers, revised heads/intake vs L05. 255 hp @ 4600 rpm / 330 lb-ft @ 2800 rpm confirmed consistent 1996-1998 (engine ran through 2002 in vans/SUVs). Matches brief exactly.
Standard dual-motor powertrain for 3WT/4WT Work Truck trims; full torque from rest with a constant-power taper above roughly 4,350 rpm.
Peak-output Silverado EV powertrain, reaching 754 hp/785 lb-ft only in the RST's 'Wide Open Watts' launch mode; constant-power taper above roughly 5,050 rpm.
Allison 10-speed since 2024; 2020-2023 used the 6L90 6-speed
2024+ figures (470 hp / 975 lb-ft); 2020-2023 made 445 hp / 910 lb-ft

L96 Vortec 6.0L V8, standard/only gas engine for K2XX HD 2015-2019. Rated 360 hp @ 5400 rpm / 380 lb-ft @ 4200 rpm (SAE net) for the entire model span. Paired exclusively with the Hydra-Matic 6L90-E 6-speed automatic and a 4.10 rear axle (GM's own 2015 consumer equipment sheet and 2016 technical spec sheet both state 4.10 is standard AND ONLY available on the Vortec 6.0L in SRW configurations; 3.73 appears in GM's tech-sheet transmission table as a theoretical alternate and does show up on some 3500HD DRW gas trailering rows, but never on 2500HD/3500HD SRW rows).

LML Duramax, 2015-2016 only (replaced by L5P for MY2017). Rated 397 hp @ 3000 rpm / 765 lb-ft @ 1600 rpm (SAE cert). Allison 1000 6-speed and 3.73 axle only, confirmed by GM's 2016 spec sheet ('Final drive ratio: 3.73' under the Allison 1000 column) and independently by a 2015 diesel LT Crew Cab 4x4 window sticker (VIN 1GC1KVE87FF151272) showing 'Rear Axle, 3.73 Ratio' as an installed $100 option over base.

L5P Duramax, 2017-2019, replaced LML for MY2017; carried the K2XX HD generation to its end in 2019 before the T1 HD redesign (MY2020) switched to the 10L1000 10-speed and a 3.42-only axle. Rated 445 hp @ 2800 rpm / 910 lb-ft @ 1600 rpm (SAE cert), still paired with the same Allison 1000 6-speed and 3.73 axle as the LML.

6.0L Vortec V8 gas, standard engine for GMT900 HD trucks; curve models the 2010-2014 L96 rating (360 hp @ 5400 rpm / 380 lb-ft @ 4200 rpm) that carried into the K2XX successor, since the earlier 2007.5-2009 LY6 was rated lower at 353 hp / 373 lb-ft on the same architecture.

6.6L Duramax V8 diesel (LMM), the sole diesel offering for MY2007.5-2010, rated 365 hp @ 3200 rpm / 660 lb-ft @ 1600 rpm (SAE) with a 3,450 rpm redline in Silverado/Sierra HD applications, paired exclusively with the Allison 1000 6-speed.

6.6L Duramax V8 diesel (LML), replacing the LMM for MY2011-2014 with SCR/DEF emissions aftertreatment added; rated 397 hp @ 3000 rpm / 765 lb-ft @ 1600 rpm (SAE) - identical rating to the later K2XX-generation LML (2015-2016), still on the Allison 1000 6-speed.
The workhorse gas V8 of the GMT800 HD line — smooth and cheap to run, but it has to work hard towing heavy loads.
GM's biggest-ever pickup gas V8 — brute-force big-block torque for towing, without a diesel's price premium.
The first-generation Duramax that put GM back in the diesel-towing conversation — later recalled for injector durability issues.
The most sought-after pre-emissions Duramax — strong power with no DPF, right before the 2007.5 LMM added one.

TBI big-block 454, RPO L19, standard 2500/3500 HD tune (distinct from the higher-output 454SS performance-truck calibration). 230 hp @ 3600 rpm / 385 lb-ft @ 1600 rpm, essentially unchanged 1988-1995 per GMT400 archival source.
Vortec 7400, RPO L29: hydraulic roller cam, MPFI (vs L19's TBI), 1996-2000. 290 hp @ 4000 rpm / 410 lb-ft @ 3200 rpm confirmed by two independent sources.

GM/Detroit Diesel 6.5L Turbo (RPO L56 1992-93 with mechanical Stanadyne DB2 pump; RPO L65 1994-2000 with electronic DS4 pump). Modeled rating: 190 hp @ 3400 rpm / 385 lb-ft @ 1800 rpm - the automatic-transmission standard-pickup figure best corroborated for the bulk of the 1994-2000 production run.
Allison 10-speed since 2024; 2020-2023 used the 6L90 6-speed
2024+ figures (470 hp / 975 lb-ft); 2020-2023 made 445 hp / 910 lb-ft

Same L96/6L90 combination as 2500HD; identical rating (360 hp @ 5400 / 380 lb-ft @ 4200) across the full 2015-2019 span. 3500HD SRW gas is 4.10-only per the same GM primary sources used for 2500HD (no separate DRW-only exception applies to SRW rows in GM's own trailering tables).
Same LML/Allison 1000 combination as 2500HD (397 hp @ 3000 / 765 lb-ft @ 1600), 2015-2016 only, 3.73-only axle.
Same L5P/Allison 1000 combination as 2500HD (445 hp @ 2800 / 910 lb-ft @ 1600), 2017-2019, last three years of the K2XX HD generation before the T1 HD redesign for MY2020.
Same L96-rated 6.0L Vortec V8 as the 2500HD (360 hp @ 5400 rpm / 380 lb-ft @ 4200 rpm), heavier-duty springs/frame on the 3500HD SRW add roughly 70kg of curb weight versus the 2500HD.
Same LMM-rated 6.6L Duramax as the 2500HD (365 hp @ 3200 rpm / 660 lb-ft @ 1600 rpm), sole diesel for MY2007.5-2010; 3500HD SRW carries roughly 65kg more curb weight than the 2500HD.
Same LML-rated 6.6L Duramax as the 2500HD (397 hp @ 3000 rpm / 765 lb-ft @ 1600 rpm), MY2011-2014; 3500HD SRW carries roughly 70kg more curb weight than the 2500HD.
Same LQ4 gas V8 as the 2500HD, in the heavier-duty 3500 SRW chassis — a lower-cost alternative to the diesel for towing.
The big-block option in the top-GVWR SRW pickup — favored by owners wanting diesel-like towing torque without diesel fuel/maintenance costs.
The 3500 SRW's most popular tow rig of this era — LB7 diesel torque on the highest-GVWR single-rear-wheel chassis.
The last pre-DPF Duramax in the top-GVWR SRW pickup — peak power/torque for this generation before 2007.5 emissions changes.

Same L19 TBI 454 as the 2500HD entry; curb weight raised for the heavier 3500 SRW crew-cab baseline (GMT400 crew cab did exist on the 3500, unlike the 1500/2500 which had no half-ton-style crew option until later platforms).
Same L29 Vortec 7400 as the 2500HD entry; curb weight raised for the 3500 SRW crew-cab baseline.

Same 6.5L Turbo Diesel (L56/L65) as the 2500HD entry, on the heavier 3500 SRW crew-cab baseline. This diesel+crew-cab combination was a common and popular GMT400 configuration among owners/collectors.
EV2X entry dual-motor trim (front + rear Ultium Drive units), available spring 2023.
EV3X / Edition 1 tri-motor flagship (1 front + 2 rear Ultium Drive units); launched as Edition 1 in Dec 2021, 3X trim added Apr 2023.
eTorque assist not modeled; returned for 2026 after a 2025 hiatus
2025+ replaces the 5.7L HEMI as the volume engine
2025+, upper trims only (3.92 axle standard)

Second-generation ("gen 3" VM Motori-derived) EcoDiesel; discontinued after MY2022. Roughly 190 lb heavier than the eTorque 5.7 HEMI in like-for-like Crew Cab 4x4 trim. Official max engine speed is 5,800 rpm (unusually high for a diesel; confirmed by two independent sources) though real-world power falls off steeply well before that governed limit.

MY2013 was rated 395 hp/407 lb-ft (548 Nm); a running change for MY2014 raised peak torque to 410 lb-ft (556 Nm, modeled here), matching the later eTorque figure. TorqueFlite 8HP70 was optional in 2013 alongside a 65RFE 6-speed (standard on base 4x2 trims); 8HP70 became the default towing-focused choice from MY2014 on, though 65RFE persisted as a lower-cost option on Tradesman/Express trims through 2018.
First-generation VM Motori EcoDiesel; launched for MY2014 only (not offered in MY2013). Standard with TorqueFlite 8HP70; roughly 260 lb heavier than the 5.7 HEMI in like-for-like Crew Cab 4x4 trim.
Updated 4.7L V8 carried the same 310 hp/330 lb-ft rating through the whole pre-refresh 4th generation; MY2012 switched it from the 545RFE to the newer 65RFE 6-speed.
New VVT (variable camshaft timing) HEMI generation with MDS cylinder deactivation from launch; carried the same 390 hp/407 lb-ft rating through the whole pre-refresh 4th generation.
Base 4.7L V8 offered across the whole generation, rated 235 hp/295 lb-ft through MY2007; a running change for MY2008 raised it to roughly 310 hp/330 lb-ft (not modeled as a separate entry here).
First-generation (non-VVT) 5.7L HEMI; introduced for MY2003 as the range-topping engine, gained cylinder-deactivation (MDS) for MY2005 with no change to peak ratings.
Carryover top engine from the 2nd-gen truck, offered only in the first two model years of the 3rd generation before the 5.7L HEMI replaced it as the range-topping V8.

220 hp @ 4400 rpm / 300 lb-ft @ 3200 rpm, unchanged 1994-2001. CORRECTION to brief: the 5.2L stayed in the light-duty Chrysler A500 transmission family the whole generation (42RE 1994-95 -> 44RE 1996-2001) -- it never moved to the larger A518-family 46RE used behind the 5.9L; the brief's '46RE from 1996?' guess was wrong. 42RE/44RE share the same A500 gearset (2.74/1.54/1.00/0.69), distinct from 46RE's 2.45/1.45/1.00/0.69. Baseline is Club Cab (extended cab) 4x4 short bed; no crew cab existed in this generation (Quad Cab from 1998 is still an extended cab).

Modeled at the dominant late-generation rating: 245 hp @ 4000 rpm / 335 lb-ft @ 3200 rpm (1997-2001; Sport Group trucks were 250 hp/345 lb-ft in the last couple of years). CORRECTION/refinement to brief: 1994-1996 trucks made less -- 230 hp / 330 lb-ft -- so the brief's '230-245 hp / 330-345 lb-ft' range is correct but understates that it's a step change around MY1997, not a smooth spread. Standard Output 6.7L Cummins with the 68RFE 6-speed automatic, rated 350 hp / 650 lb-ft — the sole automatic-transmission Cummins calibration on the 2500 in this pre-refresh era (a manual-only 350 hp/800 lb-ft High Output rating existed on the 3500 starting late MY2011, but was G56-manual-only and not offered with an automatic until the 2013 Aisin refresh, so it is excluded here).
